title: The Campfire
seo_title: Campfire Charcuterie Board: Salami Logs & Pepper Flames
description: A campfire charcuterie board for 12 to 15: salami-stick logs, standing pepper flames, little smokies and summer sausage, with cheddar and pepper jack.
hook: A campfire you can eat: salami-stick logs, pepper flames and pepperoni embers.

items.name: Dry salami sticks or snack sticks
Cream cheese plus 4 oz shredded cheddar

why: The flames are just sliced bell peppers, standing up in a base of cheese, and the logs are dry salami sticks stacked like firewood. It's an easy showpiece, rated 2 of 5.
Around the fire, cocktail sausages, summer sausage, pepperoni, cheddar, pepper jack and cheese balls feed a crowd. It suits camping parties, fall gatherings and Scout events.

timeline.what: Roast the potatoes, roll the cheese balls, and cut the pumpernickel cubes and cheese cubes.
Warm the cocktail sausages and skewer them (they can be served warm or at room temperature).
Build the fire, the stone ring, then the camp around it.
Slice the apples (toss them in lemon water) and set out the s'mores.

faq.q: How do you make a campfire charcuterie board?
faq.a: Stack salami sticks like logs, stand sliced red, orange and yellow peppers in a cheese base as flames, and scatter pepperoni as embers. Fill the rest of the board with sausages and cheese.
Yes. It's mostly mild sausages, cheddar and peppers. Cut cocktail sausages lengthwise for small children.

Make the cheese balls and cut the peppers the day before. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
